messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing per-pool headroom on us-east-dedicated-2 drop from ~28% to ~6% after the kernel selection change rolled yesterday.
liam: Hmm. Is that the change that prefers int8 kernels for long sequences? saw a small perf win in microbenchmarks but might affect batching.
maya: yes, the runtime now prefers quantized kernels for matmul when seq_len > 1024. But after rolling, token-latency p50 for chat-route increased ~18ms.
olivia: Can you paste the token-level breakdown from the dashboard? curious if the extra is in kernel exec or in the KV cache path.
maya: pasted excerpt from perf-dash: 
```
token_latency_breakdown: { queue: 4ms, kernel_exec: 27ms -> 45ms, kv_lookup: 3ms, postproc: 2ms }
per_route: { /chat: p50=92ms p95=210ms, /summarize: p50=60ms }
pool_headroom_us_east_dedicated_2: 6%
noisy_neighbor_alerts: 3 in last 6h
```
so kernel_exec jumped.
jen: we also saw sustained higher GPU utilization on node group 2 right? Ops had a noisy neighbor alert from an internal tenant that had large batched rerank jobs.
liam: Right — batching heuristics were relaxed in the same deploy: allowed batch_size up to 512 for dedicated pools to improve throughput. That interacts badly with the new kernel for long sequences (more memory thrash -> slower kernels).
olivia: can infra-bot surface per-pod kernel selection and batch sizes for the last 24h? need to correlate which pods switched to int8 kernel and which got large batches.
infra-bot: @olivia query queued: PromQL -> sum by(pod) (rate(gpu_kernel_exec_ms_sum[5m])) / sum by(pod) (rate(gpu_kernel_exec_ms_count[5m])) ; plus label batch_size, kernel_variant. Link: <https://prom.redwood.internal/graph?g=kernel_exec>
maya: also noticed KV cache hit-rate fell 2ppt on that pool after deploy; could be cache eviction due to larger KV footprints from bigger batches.
jen: noisy-neighbor detection flagged 3 pods with high steal and long tail GPU memcpy times. I can isolate them and throttle. Should we rollback the kernel selection change or tune batching heuristics first?
liam: Suggestion: pin kernel selection to prefer float16 for seq_len between 1024-2048 for dedicated pools until we fix batch memory scheduling. Quick canary: change policy on one sub-pool and watch token-level p95 for /chat.
olivia: I can deploy a canary policy and update the dedicated dashboard to add per-pod kernel_variant column + batch_size heatmap. That will help with route-level KPIs.
maya: please also add a small eval that replays yesterday's production trace (seq_len distribution + rerank bursts) against both kernels and both batching configs.
opsbot: Replay job submitted: job_id=rb-2026-03-18-91. Results will land in S3: s3://redwood-inference/replay/rb-2026-03-18-91/results.json
liam: If canary looks good we can keep quantized kernels for hosted but avoid auto-apply for dedicated pools until the scheduler handles KV working set.
jen: I'll throttle the noisy tenants for next 2 hours and create a short-lived reservation to buy headroom for the canary.
maya: thanks. Olivia, ping when dashboard update is live and when replay results are in. I'll monitor token-level latency dashboard and per-pool headroom.
olivia: will do. adding a panel: per-pod kernel_variant, batch_size, kv_hit_rate, queue_depth, token_p95_by_route. ETA ~30m.
maya: perfect. :thumbsup:
liam: quick note for follow-up: add an alert if kernel_exec_ms for dedicated pools diverges >20% from baseline for more than 10m (route-aware). prevents silent regressions.
olivia: adding to alerts list. also logging the regression to perf-regressions board with links to replay and dashboard.
jen: thanks team — doing the throttle now and opening a temporary incident channel if things worsen.
maya: closing loop later with results.
